C005.subject: Reducing class size below 20 students
C005.object: only for students from low socioeconomic backgrounds, when learning is assessed via standardized tests
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Reducing class size below 20 students only for students from low socioeconomic backgrounds, when learning is assessed via standardized tests]

[PATH:empirical] Re-analysis of data from Project STAR (Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio) with subgroup analysis by socioeconomic status using free/reduced-price lunch eligibility as proxy — Project STAR is a landmark randomized experiment on class size reduction. Re-analyzing its data to isolate effects for low-SES students on standardized test scores would directly test the hypothesis, as the original study found overall benefits but subgroup effects are disputed.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review or meta-analysis of class size reduction studies in Title I schools from 1990-2020, focusing on standardized test outcomes and socioeconomic stratification — A comprehensive meta-analysis would aggregate evidence across multiple studies, increasing statistical power to detect differential effects by SES and assess consistency of findings within the specified temporal and geographic scope.

scope.domain: empirical education research with quantifiable metrics and socioeconomic stratification

qualifier.geographic: United States public school districts with Title I funding

C006.subject: Reducing class size
C006.predicate: has a measurable positive effect on learning
C006.object: when class size is defined as fewer than 15 students and learning outcomes are defined as standardized test scores in mathematics
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Reducing class size when class size is defined as fewer than 15 students and learning outcomes are defined as standardized test scores in mathematics]

[PATH:empirical] Tennessee Student/Teacher Achievement Ratio (STAR) project data reanalysis focusing on classes with fewer than 15 students in mathematics standardized test outcomes — The STAR project is a landmark randomized experiment on class size reduction; a targeted reanalysis of the small-class condition (13-17 students) specifically for math test scores can directly test the hypothesis with high internal validity.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of class size effects on elementary mathematics achievement, e.g., by Hattie (2009) or more recent updates, filtering studies with class sizes ≤15 and standardized math test outcomes — A systematic meta-analysis focusing on the specific threshold (fewer than 15 students) and outcome (math test scores) would aggregate effect sizes across multiple studies, increasing statistical power and clarifying the disputed status.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal quasi-experimental study using administrative data from a large U.S. school district that implemented a class size reduction policy to ≤15 in early elementary grades, with propensity score matching on student demographics and prior achievement — Leveraging natural variation in policy implementation and controlling for confounders via matching can provide robust evidence on causal effects in real-world settings, addressing external validity concerns of randomized experiments.

scope.domain: empirical educational research with operationalized definitions
